items.stem: Why must a tool's description be written carefully for an agent?

options.text: The model reads it to decide when and how to call the tool
options.rationale: Correct: the description is part of the model's decision input, so it must be precise.

options.text: It is shown on the company home page
options.rationale: Tool descriptions are for the agent, not marketing.

options.text: It sets the server's memory limit
It determines the user's password policy

items.explanation: Correct: the description is part of the model's decision input, so it must be precise.

items.stem: Which TWO make a tool error useful to an agent? (Select TWO.)

options.text: A structured, actionable message the model can reason about
options.rationale: Correct: a clear structured error lets the agent recover or choose another action.

options.text: A flag indicating whether the call is safe to retry
options.rationale: Correct: retryability tells the agent whether trying again can help.

options.text: A raw stack trace with internal paths
options.rationale: Stack traces leak internals and are hard for the model to act on.
Hiding the failure makes the agent act on wrong assumptions.

items.explanation: Correct: a clear structured error lets the agent recover or choose another action.

items.stem: An agent calls a tool with an argument outside the allowed range. What should the tool do?

options.text: Reject the call with a validation error before taking any action
options.rationale: Correct: out-of-contract arguments must be validated and refused before execution.

options.text: Execute anyway and hope for the best
options.rationale: Acting on invalid input is exactly what validation prevents.

options.text: Silently clamp the value with no signal to the agent
options.rationale: Silent changes hide the problem and can corrupt results.
A single bad argument should not take down the agent.

items.explanation: Correct: out-of-contract arguments must be validated and refused before execution.
